# Core Engine Requirements Quality Checklist: Core Ledger and Merge Engine

**Purpose**: Check that the written requirements for feature 001 are complete, clear, consistent and measurable before implementation starts (author pass, standard depth).
**Created**: 2026-10-18
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

Focus areas: admission and atomicity, merge and determinism, model errors and versions, scope and traceability.

## Admission and Atomicity

- [x] CHK001 Is the two-stage rejection rule (all schema errors first, rule failures only when there are none) stated for every rejection path, including flagged requests? [Completeness, Spec §FR-007, §FR-022]
- [x] CHK002 Is "request hash" defined in the spec itself (which parts of the payload and identity it covers, and that `expected_seq` is excluded), rather than only in SPEC.md? [Clarity, Spec §FR-008]
- [x] CHK003 Are the fields of a duplicate request's response listed, so "same shape as the original success" can be checked objectively? [Measurability, Spec §FR-008, §SC-012]
- [x] CHK004 Is the retry behavior defined for a request key whose original request was rejected (nothing stored, so the retry is processed again)? [Gap, Spec §FR-008]
- [x] CHK005 Is the relationship between a request key and a per-entry idempotency key defined (when each is required, what each protects)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-008]
- [x] CHK006 Are requirements defined for two retries of the same request arriving at the same time? [Gap, Edge Case, Spec §FR-008]
- [x] CHK007 Are the permission checks for tiers (FR-006) and for the non-rejection flag (FR-022) consistent about "tier or contributor" and about which one wins when they differ? [Consistency, Ambiguity, Spec §FR-006, §FR-022]
- [x] CHK008 Are the contents of a rejection audit record stated for both modes consistently between FR-027 and SC-013? [Consistency, Spec §FR-027, §SC-013]
- [x] CHK009 Is pruning defined precisely (which record goes first, when pruning runs, how the two limits combine)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-028]
- [x] CHK010 Is the behavior defined when writing the audit record itself fails (is the rejection still returned)? [Gap, Exception Flow, Spec §FR-027]
- [x] CHK011 Are requirements defined for a storage failure part-way through committing a request, so that "none or all" still holds? [Gap, Recovery, Spec §FR-029]

## Merge and Determinism

- [x] CHK012 Is the "stable ordering of fields" in FR-019 tied to a defined canonical form, so "byte-for-byte identical" is measurable? [Clarity, Measurability, Spec §FR-019]
- [x] CHK013 Are the numeric types (decimal, float, timestamp) whose rendering must be identical across ports specified? [Gap, Spec §FR-019]
- [x] CHK014 Does the spec say what happens when a `set` writes a struct value to a field whose rule is whole-value (for example `lww` on a struct)? [Gap, Spec §FR-010]
- [x] CHK015 Are equality and ordering rules defined for the union rule ("in tier order without duplicates"), including lists of structs? [Clarity, Spec §US3 scenario 2, §FR-010]
- [x] CHK016 Is the behavior of maximum and minimum defined for values with no natural order or of mixed types? [Gap, Spec §FR-010]
- [x] CHK017 Are tombstone requirements consistent between FR-015 ("deleting a nested structure removes its subtree") and the edge case about writes beneath a deleted parent? [Consistency, Spec §FR-015, §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK018 Is the default and delete behavior specified for children of a struct (a per-child default after a delete)? [Gap, Spec §FR-014, §FR-016]
- [x] CHK019 Is it stated in the requirements, not only in assumptions, that tiers are defined by the schema and one order applies to every field? [Consistency, Spec §FR-009, §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK020 Can SC-001 be judged as written, given the worked example in SPEC.md also contains computed and deferred values that this feature leaves out of scope? [Measurability, Ambiguity, Spec §SC-001, §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK021 Are requirements defined for an existing entry whose tier no longer exists after a schema change? [Gap, Edge Case, Spec §FR-009]

## Model Errors and Versions

- [x] CHK022 Is a model error's identity ("rule and path scope") defined in the spec, together with the accepted limitation that a worsening error is not detected? [Clarity, Spec §FR-024, §FR-023]
- [x] CHK023 Is attribution to "the request that introduced it" defined for errors found only on re-derivation under a new schema version? [Clarity, Spec §FR-030, §FR-026]
- [x] CHK024 Are FR-024 and the edge case about fixing one error while adding another consistent about judging the net effect of the whole request? [Consistency, Spec §FR-024, §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK025 Is "schema or validation-rule version" in FR-026 defined (what counts as a version change, and how a change is detected)? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-026]
- [x] CHK026 Are requirements defined for reading a document whose schema version is inactive or pinned? [Gap, Spec §FR-026]
- [x] CHK027 Are requirements defined for model errors whose path has since been deleted or removed from the document? [Gap, Edge Case, Spec §FR-025]
- [x] CHK028 Is the behavior defined when re-deriving a document fails (a validator reports a fault rather than a violation)? [Gap, Exception Flow, Spec §FR-026]
- [x] CHK029 Is an optional reason on a flagged request mentioned in the spec, given the clarification that one may be supplied? [Completeness, Spec §Clarifications, §FR-022]

## Scope and Traceability

- [x] CHK030 Is FR-031 (derived-field writes rejected) consistent with the statement that computed and deferred fields are out of scope? [Consistency, Spec §FR-031, §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK031 Do the tasks cite requirement and success-criterion IDs, so that coverage of each FR and SC can be checked? [Traceability, Gap]
- [x] CHK032 Is SC-006 measurable as written ("a typical reader"): are the hardware, cold or cached read, and request granularity defined? [Ambiguity, Measurability, Spec §SC-006]
- [x] CHK033 Are the success criteria numbered in a consistent order, with no gaps or out-of-order IDs? [Consistency, Spec §Success Criteria]
- [x] CHK034 Is the term "non-rejection flag" mapped to the name used in the interfaces (`lenient`)? [Consistency, Spec §Key Entities]
- [x] CHK035 Are the SPEC.md sections this feature depends on listed, so a SPEC change is checked against this spec? [Dependency, Gap, Spec §header]
- [x] CHK036 Is the single-logical-writer assumption tied to a requirement for what happens if two writers collide (the sequence conflict outcome)? [Assumption, Gap, Spec §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK037 Is the contributor identity input (id and permitted tiers) defined as a requirement rather than only an assumption? [Dependency, Spec §Assumptions]

## Notes

- Check items off as you review them. Items marked [Gap] or [Ambiguity] may lead to edits in `spec.md`.
- The built-in `requirements.md` checklist from `/speckit-specify` predates FR-031, request keys, staged reasons and the metadata-only mode; it was not changed by this run.
